# Procurement Recommendation

**Purchase quantity requested:** 10,000 units
**Constraints given:** none stated (this is a revision of the earlier 20,000-unit run; user requested a fresh 10,000-unit analysis)
**Generated by:** Main Procurement Agent, consulting `cost-analyst`, `performance-analyst`, and `risk-analyst` subagents
**Data source:** `data/suppliers.csv` only (5 suppliers) — no figures invented

## 1. Cost Analyst Findings

**Price ranking (cheapest to most expensive):**

| Rank | Supplier | Unit Price | Capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Supplier D | $10.75 | 10,000 |
| 2 | Supplier B | $11.20 | 8,000 |
| 3 | Supplier A | $12.50 | 5,000 |
| 4 | Supplier E | $12.90 | 4,500 |
| 5 | Supplier C | $13.80 | 3,000 |

Combined capacity across all 5 suppliers = 30,500 units (well above the 10,000-unit requirement). Supplier D is the only single supplier whose capacity (10,000) could cover the whole order alone. Price spread: $3.05/unit between cheapest (D) and most expensive (C), about 28%.

## 2. Performance Analyst Findings

| Supplier | Quality Score | OTIF % | Lead Time (Days) | Capacity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supplier A | 8.5 | 92 | 14 | 5,000 |
| Supplier B | 7.2 | 85 | 21 | 8,000 |
| Supplier C | 9.1 | 97 | 10 | 3,000 |
| Supplier D | 6.5 | 78 | 28 | 10,000 |
| Supplier E | 8.8 | 90 | 16 | 4,500 |

- Best performer: **Supplier C** — tops Quality (9.1), OTIF (97%), and Lead Time (10 days), but has the smallest capacity (3,000, only 30% of this order).
- Worst performer: **Supplier D** — weakest on Quality (6.5), OTIF (78%), and Lead Time (28 days) of any supplier, yet has the largest capacity (10,000 — enough to cover the whole order alone).
- Middle tier: Supplier A is solid across the board; Supplier E is close behind A; Supplier B is weaker on quality/OTIF/lead-time than A or E but offers more capacity.

## 5. Total Procurement Cost

**$122,325.00** for 10,000 units — average $12.2325/unit.

## 6. Key Trade-offs and Risks

- **Supplier D excluded on purpose.** D is the cheapest ($10.75/unit) and has enough capacity (10,000) to fulfill the entire order alone — but it is also rated **High risk** and is the weakest performer on every quality/service dimension (lowest Quality Score, lowest OTIF %, longest Lead Time). Because the four non-D suppliers together have 20,500 units of capacity — more than double this 10,000-unit order — there was no need to accept D's risk/quality trade-off just to hit volume.
- **Cost of avoiding D:** an allocation leaning on D (e.g., D up to capacity or a large D-heavy mix) would price out cheaper, but this plan accepts a premium in exchange for zero High-risk exposure and a stronger overall quality/OTIF/lead-time profile.
- **Concentration flag:** Supplier B carries the largest single share (40%) and is rated Medium risk. Combined, Medium-risk suppliers (B + E) hold 62.5% of the order, versus 37.5% with Low-risk suppliers (A + C). Not a single-source risk (spread across 4 suppliers), and no High-risk exposure (D at 0%).
- **Capacity buffer:** none of the four used suppliers are pinned at 100% of capacity this time (unlike the earlier 20,000-unit run) — A has 2,500 of 5,000 headroom left unused, B has 4,000 of 8,000 unused, E has 2,250 of 4,500 unused, C has 1,250 of 3,000 unused — so there is meaningful slack to absorb demand upside if needed.

## 7. Files / Subagents Used

- Data file: `data/suppliers.csv` (sole source of supplier facts — no external or invented data)
- Subagents consulted: `cost-analyst`, `performance-analyst`, `risk-analyst` (each read `data/suppliers.csv` directly)
- Orchestrator: Main Procurement Agent (`.claude/commands/procurement-decision.md`), which combined the three subagent reports, proposed this allocation, and re-verified cost and risk on the final split via `cost-analyst` and `risk-analyst` before writing this report.
